title: One fish, two volumes
hook: Changing volume can change a force.

doesNotKnow: In a toy model with fish mass and water density fixed, which bladder size displaces more water?

misconception: The first explanation of an aquatic animal feature must be correct.
objective: In a toy model with fish mass and water density fixed, which bladder size displaces more water?

claims.text: In a toy model with fish mass and water density fixed, which bladder size displaces more water? In this simplified comparison, fish mass and water density stay fixed while the illustrated overall volume changes. The larger volume displaces more water and increases buoyant force, all else equal. Real fish regulate gases and are more complex than this model.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, animal respiration and osmoregulation, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e

claims.text: The two panels are simplified schematics, not observations or measurements.
A fixed-mass object in the same water expands and displaces more water. What happens to its buoyant force? Displacing more of the same fluid increases buoyant force in this model.
